title: Yeasty Silky Korean Egg Rolls Gyoza
description: Indulgent Korean dish featuring yeasty egg rolls, topped with crispy bonito shavings and a hint of Mediterranean flair.
instructions: Combine yeast and warm water in a small bowl. Let it sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Roll out the gyoza wrappers to your desired thickness.
In a large mixing bowl, combine ground pork, chopped scallions, sesame oil, soy sauce, granulated sugar, salt, and black pepper. Mix until well combined.
Add the yeast mixture to the pork mixture and mix until smooth.
Place a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of each gyoza wrapper.
Dip your finger in a small amount of water and run it along the edges of the wrapper. Fold the wrapper over the filling to form a half-moon shape, pressing the edges together to seal the gyoza.
Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Add 1-2 tablespoons of oil to the skillet and swirl it around to coat the bottom.
When the oil is hot, add the gyoza to the skillet, leaving some space between each gyoza.
Cook the gyoza for 2-3 minutes on each side, until they are golden brown and crispy.
Remove the gyoza from the skillet and place them on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Top the gyoza with crispy bonito shavings and serve hot.
Cook pork to an internal temperature of 63°C / 145°F and let it rest for 3 minutes before serving.
